headline: Carry each node’s depth on the stack
statement: Return the largest number of nodes on any path from the root to a leaf. An empty tree has depth zero.
intuition: Depth counts nodes along a path, so carry a depth with each node and remember the greatest depth visited. An explicit stack also handles a very skewed tree.
approach: Put (root,1) on a stack if root exists.
Pop a node and depth, update the largest depth.
Push existing children with depth+1; stop when the stack is empty.
correctness: Every node is pushed once with its exact root-to-node depth because each child increases its parent depth by one. Every longest path ends at a visited leaf, so the maximum visited depth is exactly the maximum tree depth.
bruteForce: Enumerate and copy every root-to-leaf path, then measure lengths; repeatedly copying paths can cost O(n*h).

complexity.explanation: Time O(n); auxiliary space O(h). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Depth counts nodes rather than edges.
The empty tree has zero depth.
Recursive Python implementations can exceed recursion limits on long chains.
